haiku-low.q1: The scheduler's 02:00 UTC fire, or a retry 15 minutes after a failed attempt. It extracts app orders rows with updated_at from (high-water mark minus 2h) up to the replica's current time.
haiku-low.q2: A bulk import stamps updated_at when the row is written, not when the transaction commits. So a row can become visible up to 90 minutes after its updated_at.
haiku-low.q3: A later nightly extract re-reads it through the 2-hour lookback. The merge overwrites the stored row because its updated_at is greater than or equal to the stored one.
haiku-low.q4: Nothing is removed. The warehouse keeps the row and sets is_deleted = true, because the app sets deleted_at.
haiku-low.q5: The run is marked failed and a new attempt starts 15 minutes later. After a third failure, on-call is paged and there are no more retries that night.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards refresh at 06:00 anyway and show last night's complete but older data. The 06:00 check posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. If that Sunday's load succeeded and a creation day's count or checksum differs, it reloads that day's orders from the replica.
haiku-low.q8: The merge keeps only the highest updated_at per order_id. It overwrites an existing fact row only if the staged updated_at is greater than or equal to the stored one.
haiku-low.q9: In the single etl_watermark row. The value written is window_end, set in the same warehouse transaction as the merge, at commit (step 4d).
haiku-low.q10: The merge, the watermark update and the run marked succeeded all commit in one warehouse transaction. A failure rolls all of it back, so dashboards never see a half-loaded night.
haiku-low.q11: Staged data from the failed attempt is discarded, because the next attempt empties stg_orders. The retry extracts from the unchanged mark minus 2h up to a new window_end.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads all of that mismatched creation day's orders from the replica into stg_orders. It merges them with rules 4(a) to (c) in one transaction, and does not move the high-water mark.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler fires at 02:00 UTC (or a retry 15 min after a failed attempt). It extracts every order with updated_at in the window from (high-water mark minus 2 hours) up to the replica's current time (window_end), read from the app's Postgres read replica.
sonnet.q2: A bulk import stamps updated_at when the row is written, not when the transaction commits, so the row can become visible up to 90 minutes after its updated_at.
sonnet.q3: The app sets updated_at to the write time, so the edited order falls in a later night's extract window. It is staged and merged into fact_orders, overwriting the stored row if staged updated_at >= stored updated_at.
sonnet.q4: The app sets deleted_at (the row is never removed) and updated_at is bumped. The delete is extracted like any change; the warehouse keeps the row and sets is_deleted = true (is_deleted = deleted_at is not null).
sonnet.q5: The scheduler marks the run failed and starts a new attempt 15 minutes later, starting again at step 1. Max 3 attempts; the third failure pages on-call and there are no more retries that night. If it failed in the merge, the transaction rolls back and fact_orders and the mark are unchanged.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards refresh at 06:00 regardless and show last night's data (complete but old). The 06:00 check finds no succeeded run for tonight and posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts. (On-call is paged only if the third attempt failed.)
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation: it compares per-creation-day count and checksum (order_id plus updated_at) between the replica and fact_orders for the last 30 days, reloads mismatched days into stg_orders and merges them into fact_orders. This only runs if that Sunday's nightly load succeeded.
sonnet.q8: In the merge, per order_id only the staged row with the highest updated_at is kept, and an existing fact_orders row is overwritten only if the staged updated_at is greater than or equal to the stored one. So an older copy never replaces a newer one.
sonnet.q9: In the etl_watermark table in the warehouse (one row). It is set to window_end (the replica's current time at extract) in step 4(d), inside the same warehouse transaction as the merge and the run being marked succeeded, i.e. at commit, after the data has loaded.
sonnet.q10: The merge into fact_orders, the high-water mark advance and marking the run succeeded all happen in one warehouse transaction, so dashboards never see a half-loaded night (a failed merge rolls back).
sonnet.q11: The staged data is discarded: the retry's step 3 empties stg_orders and loads afresh. The retry extracts from the same mark (it has not moved) minus 2 hours up to the replica's current time at that retry, so the window_end is new.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads all of that day's orders (by creation day) from the replica for each day whose count or checksum differs, loads them into stg_orders, and merges with the same rules as step 4(a) to (c) in one transaction. It does not change the high-water mark.
